answer: A stake-weighted reputation market makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral behind a single verified identity before its work is paid, like an opal set in one mesa rather than scattered pebbles. If graders catch fabricated attestations, the stake is slashed and the identity burned, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes. Honest agents drift in like a zephyr, paying almost nothing, while an attacker must fund every fake at full price.
